scope: Pinned vendor source and prepared-composer coverage audit; no firmware source was changed

tx_rx/wdev_rx.c.observation: The normal management receive path passes pRxBlk->wcid and the full frame to REPORT_MGMT_FRAME_TO_MLME. FT action provenance can therefore bind the receive WCID and Addr1-derived BSS before queueing; the queued element still needs to preserve both.

common/ft_iocl.c.observation: The native FT-over-DS simulation creates an associated peer, builds an action frame addressed to that peer BSS, and enters the same general receive enqueue with its station AID. An FT-only receive stamp must preserve this supported synthetic producer.

mgmt/mgmt_entrytb.c.observation: MacTableInsertEntry does not reject a duplicate MAC before choosing a free slot; it appends the new entry to the MAC hash. The native FT BT_REQ global MacTableLookup can therefore select an unrelated-BSS duplicate. BSS-scoped lookup remains necessary even when preserving new-peer insertion. MacTableInsertEntry acquires MacTabLock internally and assigns the selected BSS/wdev and MAC under that lock; a caller-side claim followed by calling this function leaves a race window. Safe integration requires the ticket claim inside the same insertion critical section while preserving existing bookkeeping.

common/rtmp_init.c.observation: RTMPInitAdapter zeroes MacTab and initializes MacTabLock; ledger storage must be initialized exactly once at this point before queue ingress.

findings: Native common/action.c maps FT_CATEGORY_BSS_TRANSITION to FT_FtAction; MlmeEnqueueForRecv classifies the frame and the MLME dispatcher sends ACTION_STATE_MACHINE directly to the handler.
The current association-generation capture helper returns a zero stamp for every machine except WPA_STATE_MACHINE, and its dequeue stale check likewise only validates WPA events.
The prepared explicit FT enqueue is currently called only from the FT_RrbHandler composition. Ordinary over-air FT action receive is not stamped by that composition.

The native terminating FT_ACTION_BT_REQ branch can MacTableInsertEntry after dequeue when no peer exists. The prepared RRB composition instead requires an active peer in the destination BSS and returns before allocation/enqueue when none matches. This follows the user's explicit early-return rule but its effect on first-peer and forwarded-RRB behavior remains to be resolved against product requirements.

After successful FT_AuthReqHandler, native FT_FtAction writes MdIeInfo, AuthState=AS_AUTH_OPEN and Sst=SST_AUTH. Current prepared FT binding does not advance assoc_gen at this transition or refresh its live scope stamp.
The target TU result in OPTIONAL1431 covers only the prepared RRB path and cloned explicit MLME enqueue; it does not establish ordinary RX coverage or generation advancement.

Call-site audit found three producer families for MlmeEnqueueForRecv: received management frames in wdev_rx.c, an FT_RrbHandler synthetic action, and FT_OverDs_SimReq. The latter two have different provenance origins; any ordinary-action stamping must cover both without trusting a MAC-only lookup. The real first-time/unknown-peer BT_REQ insertion path remains unresolved and must not be silently removed.

Pinned mgmt_entrytb.c MacTableInsertEntry selects the first free WCID and appends the entry to the MAC hash without a duplicate-address search. A direct FT BT_REQ with no matching target-BSS station may legitimately insert a duplicate MAC on the target BSS; the native global MacTableLookup is then ambiguous and can choose the foreign BSS entry. Safe preservation must combine target-BSS insertion with a generation/pending identity that cannot be adopted by an older queued event.

The pending identity ledger now includes a standalone one-shot claim/unclaim primitive. Pinned MacTableInsertEntry owns MacTabLock internally, so an external claim then native insert is not atomic; an in-lock insertion hook/refactor is required.
next: Integrate ledger storage at adapter initialization and reserve/release tickets across exact MLME enqueue/dequeue/dispatch, restart, and destroy paths. Preserve native BT_REQ first-peer insertion through an in-lock target-BSS insertion hook that claims the ticket atomically; never use a global MAC-only fallback. Then resolve FT_AUTH generation handoff and asynchronous IAPP completion correlation before target recompilation.

contract: BSS+MAC key; same-key events share one ticket generation and increment references
claim is one-shot under caller-owned MacTabLock; second claim and same-key reservation while claimed fail
failed insertion may unclaim the exact current ticket for retry
successful insertion retires the exact BSS+MAC so all sibling queued tickets become stale
retirement prevents current checks while retaining the slot until every queued/active reference releases
slot reuse advances a nonzero generation; an old token cannot release or adopt the reused slot
generation overflow poisons only that slot
